The mailbox belonged to Mrs. Gable down the street, she had these beautiful petunias planted all around the base of it. She was out there crying over her crushed flowers for an hour. But yeah, the guy at the store was just being slow and I ended up yelling at him to just type the numbers in, and I felt bad later, but in the moment I just get so irritable when people can't keep up with me.\n\nDoctor: Do you find that your racing thoughts are getting in the way of your daily activities or relationships?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I guess they are. It's like I can't hold onto a thought long enough to finish a task. \n\nSpeaking of chores, I was supposed to fix the leaky faucet in the guest bathroom last week. The drip, drip, drip was driving me crazy. It sounded like a metronome, you know? My old piano teacher, Mrs. Higgins, used to use a metronome. She had this dusty old upright piano that smelled like mothballs and peppermint. She always kept a bowl of those red and white peppermints on top of it. I hated those things, they always stuck to my teeth. One time, I lost a filling chewing on one. The dentist I went to had this huge fish tank in the waiting room with these neon tetras that would just dart around. I could watch them for hours, just zipping back and forth. But yeah, I've also been pulling back from my church friends, and honestly, I'm starting to worry if I can even safely go back to my caregiving work with my head spinning like this.\n\nDoctor: Have you recently experienced a period where you felt abnormally happy or irritable and had lots of energy?\n\nPatient: Yeah, definitely. No, not at all. When I'm fired up like that, I really don't need much sleep. I can sleep maybe two or three hours and wake up way before dawn, just feeling completely ready to go. I don't even think anything is wrong with it, you know? I'll just be up making all these plans while the house is still pitch dark. 

Well, dark except for the streetlight out front. It flickers a lot. It's got this orange glow, like a sodium lamp or something. The city came out to fix it once, but the guy brought the wrong bulb. He was driving this big bucket truck that had a squeaky hydraulic lift. It sounded exactly like the old screen door at my very first apartment. That place was so drafty, the wind would just howl through the window frames in the winter. I tried taping them up with duct tape, but the tape just got all hot in the summer and left this gross gray residue everywhere. It took me three days with a bottle of solvent and a putty knife to get it off when I finally moved out. The landlord was a real stickler about the security deposit, he tried to charge me for a carpet stain that was there before I even moved in. 

But yeah, I just don't feel tired at all. I can run on just a couple hours of sleep and feel totally fine making my plans while everyone else is still in bed.

I had a buddy who bought a snake once, and... wait, what did you ask me again?\n\nDoctor: Do you hear your name being called or voices when you're not alone, like during the staff meeting?\n\nPatient: No, no, not during the meeting. Like I said, it's just when I'm alone. Like if I'm walking down the hallway at work and nobody's around, or if I'm at home, near the laundry room. I'll just hear somebody say my name, or I'll hear one of the residents yelling out for help. Clear as a bell, I swear. I always go looking, thinking somebody fell or something, but the hallway is just empty. \n\nIt's just like that time I thought I heard my dog barking outside, but I don't even own a dog anymore. I used to have a beagle mix named Buster. Best dog ever, but he had this terrible habit of digging under the fence. I must've patched that chain-link a dozen times with chicken wire and zip ties. You ever try cutting chicken wire with regular scissors? It ruins them. My ex-wife was so mad when she found out I used her good fabric scissors for it. She was a seamstress, made all these custom curtains for people. Velvet, silk, you name it. She made this one set of drapes that weighed like fifty pounds, I had to use heavy-duty anchors just to get the rod into the drywall. Drywall anchors are a scam, though, if you ask me. Half the time they just spin in the hole and you end up with a bigger mess than you started with. But yeah, no, at the meeting it was just me and the chairs.\n\nDoctor: Do you hear your name being called or voices every time you're alone, or does it happen only sometimes?\n\nPatient: Well, it's not every single time I'm alone, no. Just sometimes. Like I said, I'll just be by the laundry room or walking down an empty hallway on shift, and I'll hear my name, or a resident yelling for help. Clear as day. But it's not all the time. \n\nI mean, if it was all the time, I'd probably go crazy, right? Especially at work. Working the night shift is already so quiet, except for the ice machine at the end of the hall. That thing is so loud when it drops a new batch of ice. It sounds like rocks falling on a tin roof. I tried telling maintenance about it, but they never listen. The maintenance guy, Carl, he's always too busy fixing the golf carts they use to drive the bigwigs around the campus. They got these fancy electric ones now, but they used to have gas ones that smelled like a lawnmower. Reminds me of when I used to mow lawns in the summer back in high school. I saved up enough to buy this beat-up old Honda Civic, but the muffler fell off like two weeks after I bought it. Sounded like a tank driving down the street. The neighbors hated me. But yeah, it just happens sometimes.\n\nDoctor: When you're hearing your name being called or the residents yelling for help, do you feel like you need to do something in response?\n\nPatient: Yeah, definitely. I mean, if someone is yelling for help, I have to go see what's going on. So when I'm alone in that hallway on shift, or at home by the laundry room, and I hear my name or a resident calling out clear as day, I always go check. I go looking right away, but... there isn't anybody there. It's just empty. \n\nBut you have to check, you know? It's a safety thing. It's like checking the lint trap on the dryer. You're supposed to do it every single load, but people get lazy. My cousin Danny got lazy with his, and his whole laundry room caught on fire a few years back. Melted the linoleum right to the subfloor. The fire department had to smash his big front bay window just to drag the hose inside. Cost him an absolute fortune to replace that glass. It was one of those custom tinted ones because he lived on a corner lot and didn't want people looking in at him eating dinner. He used to eat dinner on this ugly brown velvet couch right in the living room. The firemen soaked the couch completely with the hoses. Honestly, they did him a favor, that thing was hideous and it always smelled like wet pennies. But yeah, I always go look when I hear them, just in case.\n\nDoctor: Do you often find it hard to stay on one topic when talking to someone?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I guess I do. It's just... my mind goes so fast, you know? It jumps from my job, to church, to my wife, to all these new workshop ideas I have. It goes so fast that I actually lose the very first thought before I can even get the words out right. \n\nSpeaking of workshops, I was thinking about building this new workbench. You need a really solid top for a good workbench, like a thick butcher block. My uncle had this massive butcher block out in his garage. He used to process his own deer meat out there during hunting season. He'd make this spicy deer jerky that would just burn your mouth up, but you couldn't stop eating it. He used this old dehydrator that sounded like a jet engine taking off. My aunt hated that thing because it would vibrate through the wall and rattle the shelves in the kitchen, and it would knock her ceramic frogs out of place. She collected those little green ceramic frogs, had hundreds of them all over the house. Dusting them took her practically all day Sunday. She wouldn't let anybody else touch them because she was afraid we'd chip the paint. But yeah, my thoughts just kind of race around like that and I lose track of what I was trying to say in the first place.\n\nDoctor: Do you find your mind racing and thoughts jumping around like this when you're relaxed and not in a situation like the staff meeting?\n\nPatient: Yeah, even when I'm just sitting on the couch trying to unwind. It's exactly like I was just saying a minute ago—my brain will still just jump from work, to what's happening at church, to my wife, to those workshop ideas. It goes so fast I still lose the first thought before I can even get it out, even if I'm just hanging out talking to my wife in the living room. \n\nWe were sitting there the other night, just trying to watch a movie to relax. It was one of those old Westerns. My dad used to love Westerns. He had this huge collection of VHS tapes down in his basement. Hundreds of them, all lined up on these flimsy particle-board shelves he built himself. One time, the dog bumped into the bottom shelf and the whole thing came crashing down. Tapes went everywhere. The dog—he was this goofy golden retriever named Buster—he got so scared he hid under the kitchen table for three hours. Wouldn't even come out for a piece of cheese. He loved American cheese, the kind individually wrapped in that clear plastic. You'd unwrap a slice and he'd come running from a mile away just hearing the plastic crinkle. He was a good dog, though, lived to be fourteen. But yeah, even when I'm supposed to be completely relaxed, my mind is still doing that jumping around thing.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel anxious or upset when your mind is racing like that?\n\nPatient: No, I wouldn't really say anxious... it's more like... there are these stretches where I just feel so bright and fired up, you know? Like everything is finally lining up perfectly and I've got all the answers. It feels great, honestly. But then, if someone tries to slow me down or they question what I'm doing, I just snap. I snap way harder than I mean to. \n\nLike the other day at the hardware store, the guy at the register was taking forever to ring up my lumber. He kept scanning this one barcode over and over, and the machine kept making this loud, obnoxious beep. It sounded exactly like the backup alarm on a garbage truck. They come down my street every Tuesday morning at 5:30 AM, right when I'm trying to get my last hour of sleep. The driver always revs the engine right outside my bedroom window. He drives this huge green truck with a dented bumper. I saw him hit a mailbox once, just backed right into it and kept going like nothing happened. The mailbox belonged to Mrs. Gable down the street, she had these beautiful petunias planted all around the base of it. She was out there crying over her crushed flowers for an hour. But yeah, the guy at the store was just being slow and I ended up yelling at him to just type the numbers in, and I felt bad later, but in the moment I just get so irritable when people can't keep up with me.\n\nDoctor: Do you find that your racing thoughts are getting in the way of your daily activities or relationships?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I guess they are. I mean, they put me on leave from the senior center where I work as an aide, which is frustrating. And my wife... she's been having to remind me about chores and appointments because I'm just not keeping up the way I used to. It's like I can't hold onto a thought long enough to finish a task. \n\nSpeaking of chores, I was supposed to fix the leaky faucet in the guest bathroom last week. The drip, drip, drip was driving me crazy. It sounded like a metronome, you know? My old piano teacher, Mrs. Higgins, used to use a metronome. She had this dusty old upright piano that smelled like mothballs and peppermint. She always kept a bowl of those red and white peppermints on top of it. I hated those things, they always stuck to my teeth. One time, I lost a filling chewing on one. The dentist I went to had this huge fish tank in the waiting room with these neon tetras that would just dart around. I could watch them for hours, just zipping back and forth. But yeah, I've also been pulling back from my church friends, and honestly, I'm starting to worry if I can even safely go back to my caregiving work with my head spinning like this.\n\nDoctor: Have you recently experienced a period where you felt abnormally happy or irritable and had lots of energy?\n\nPatient: Yeah, definitely. When I get those stretches where I'm just fired up, the energy is unbelievable. I mean, on those high-energy days, I'll be up cleaning out all the closets, reorganizing everything. I'll rewrite all the care checklists for work, even though I'm on leave, and start planning this massive health fair for the church. I'll be calling people before breakfast because it feels like it all just has to happen right then, you know? \n\nBreakfast... you know, I used to love going to this little diner downtown for breakfast. It was called Mabel's. They had the best blueberry pancakes. The blueberries were always huge, like the size of marbles. I swallowed a marble once when I was a kid. It was one of those clear ones with the little swirl of color in the middle—a cat's eye, I think they called them. My mom freaked out, rushed me to the emergency room in our old station wagon. That car had the fake wood paneling on the sides. It was peeling off near the back tire. My brother used to pick at it when we were on long road trips. We drove all the way to Mount Rushmore once in that car. Took three days. The air conditioning was broken, so we had to roll the windows down, and the wind was so loud you couldn't even hear the radio. But yeah, I just get so much energy and try to do a million things at once.\n\nDoctor: When you're feeling really fired up and have lots of energy, do you find that you still need to sleep as much as you usually do?\n\nPatient: No, not at all. When I'm fired up like that, I really don't need much sleep. I can sleep maybe two or three hours and wake up way before dawn, just feeling completely ready to go. I don't even think anything is wrong with it, you know? I'll just be up making all these plans while the house is still pitch dark. \n\nWell, dark except for the streetlight out front. It flickers a lot. It's got this orange glow, like a sodium lamp or something. The city came out to fix it once, but the guy brought the wrong bulb. He was driving this big bucket truck that had a squeaky hydraulic lift. It sounded exactly like the old screen door at my very first apartment. That place was so drafty, the wind would just howl through the window frames in the winter. I tried taping them up with duct tape, but the tape just got all hot in the summer and left this gross gray residue everywhere. It took me three days with a bottle of solvent and a putty knife to get it off when I finally moved out. The landlord was a real stickler about the security deposit, he tried to charge me for a carpet stain that was there before I even moved in. \n\nBut yeah, I just don't feel tired at all. I can run on just a couple hours of sleep and feel totally fine making my plans while everyone else is still in bed.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of time where you felt extremely happy or irritable and had lots of energy that lasted for several days or longer?\n\nPatient: Yeah, definitely. My grandpa had this old aluminum canoe we'd take out. It was dented on one side from when my uncle hit a submerged log during a flood back in '93. That flood washed out the whole main bridge into town. People were taking rowboats to the grocery store. The grocery store was owned by Mr. Henderson, and he always gave out free slices of bologna at the deli counter. I haven't had bologna in years.
